headline: Zig Makes HTML Templates Type-Safe
lede: Compile templates during `zig build`. `zt` checks parameters, escapes dynamic content, validates URLs, and writes directly to `std.Io.Writer`—a compact path to safer server-rendered applications.

headline: Offshore Paperwork Moves Abramovich’s Wealth
lede: An investigation alleges that Deloitte Cyprus and MeritServus backdated documents and shifted billions through offshore entities. The firms deny wrongdoing; the paper trail is now the story.

headline: Your Browser Leaves a Durable Signature
lede: Cookies are only one way to be recognized. GPU behavior, fonts, audio rendering, screen geometry, and other signals can combine into a fingerprint that survives clearing, VPNs, and private windows.

headline: Fast Storage Lets Postgres Breathe
lede: In a 3.3-billion-row workload, local NVMe reached 16,030 transactions per second against 1,734 on baseline cloud storage. The benchmark makes an old systems lesson concrete: waiting on I/O can look like a database problem.

headline: Total Annihilation Finds New Ground
lede: An open-source engine brings the classic strategy game to modern Windows, macOS, Linux, and the browser. Its clean-room implementation preserves the machinery while leaving original assets with the owners who supplied them.

headline: An iPad Runs Linux’s AMD Driver
lede: LemonSeed Studio embeds upstream `amdgpu` and `amdkfd` inside an iPad app through PCIDriverKit. Add a Thunderbolt enclosure and a custom inference engine, and the tablet becomes an unlikely host for desktop-class GPU work.

headline: Calculus Learns to Compute
lede: This open textbook teaches introductory calculus through Julia, moving among graphical, numerical, algebraic, and verbal views. The language is not decoration: it turns exploration and visualization into part of the mathematical argument.

headline: Mapping the Mapmakers of North Korea
lede: This interactive project follows the people, sources, and compromises behind maps of one of the world’s least accessible countries. The map becomes a record not only of geography, but of uncertainty and persistence.

headline: PlayStation 2 Games Recompile for WebAssembly
lede: Static recompilation turns selected PS2 executables into C++ and WebAssembly, with a reimplemented operating system and WebGPU renderer underneath. Gran Turismo 4 and God of War II now boot in browsers—provided players bring their own discs.

headline: Holography Found Its Smaller Future
lede: Holography did not become the living-room display once imagined. Its demanding optics, costly data requirements, and narrow viewing conditions pushed it instead toward security, microscopy, measurement, art, and specialized research.
pullquote: A technology can miss its grand debut and still find useful work.
